answer: Each agent must post a bonded identity deposit before it can transact, and voting weight scales with the square root of that locked stake. So standing up a willow-thin fleet of cheap sybils yields diminishing influence: to out-vote an ocean of honest agents you must lock real capital per identity. Any identity caught faking is slashed to the nadir, forfeiting its bond. The marginal cost climbs faster than the marginal power gained, so the attacker drowns before swaying the ledger.
